objectives.understand: How the week's moves apply to your next step: a job, a proposal or a lesson.
objectives.do: Use AI to produce a real work product in your track, truthfully and checked.
objectives.demonstrate: Spot job-scam red flags, keep AI drafts truthful, and verify materials before you use them.
objectives.apply: Finish one piece of work you actually owe someone, done faster and checked by you.

discover.title: Mission briefing: your next move
discover.scenario: Three people, one week. Blessing is applying for an operations role in Port Harcourt. Musa owes a donor concept note by Thursday. Mrs Okoro needs next week's Primary 4 lesson on fractions. They all use the same moves you have learned: real material, a clear reader, the right format, and verification. Pick your track; the missions cover all three.

keyIdeas: Truthful first: AI may rephrase your experience but must never invent achievements or figures.
Any recruitment fee means walk away. Verify the employer independently.
AI proposes, you decide: check every indicator, figure and answer before it leaves your hands.

missions.title: Run the job-scam check
missions.scenario: Blessing gets a WhatsApp message: 'Congratulations! You are shortlisted for Operations Officer at a major oil company. Salary ₦850,000/month. Pay ₦15,000 for training materials to confirm your interview. Contact hr.majoroil@gmail.com.'

options.text: She is asked to pay ₦15,000 for training materials.
options.feedback: Red flag. No genuine employer charges a recruitment or training fee. Any fee means walk away.

options.text: A big company is hiring from a Gmail address.
options.feedback: Red flag. Large employers use their own domains. Verify the company and a real contact.

options.text: The salary is far above the market rate for the role, with no proper interview.
options.feedback: Red flag. That is the oldest bait there is.

options.text: The message names the role she applied for.
options.feedback: Not a red flag on its own: genuine recruiters name roles too. It's the fee, the address and the salary that give it away.

missions.hint: The lesson lists three fixed rules: fees, verifying the company, and salaries that are too good.
missions.support: Check the message against each rule. Is money requested? Can you verify who is sending it? Is the offer believable for the role?
missions.explain: A fee, an unverifiable Gmail address and a too-good salary are each enough to walk away. AI can help you check, but these rules don't change.

missions.title: Keep the draft honest
missions.scenario: Musa's field notes say: 'Two sessions held; 18 attendees at the first and 16 at the second; repeat attendance unknown.' The AI drafted results for his concept note.
missions.prompt: Which results sentence can Musa safely submit to the donor?

options.text: The programme reached 34 community members across two sessions.
options.feedback: Not safe. 34 is attendances, not people. Some may have come twice; the notes say repeat attendance is unknown.

options.text: Two sessions recorded 34 attendances; the number of unique participants has not been established.
options.feedback: Yes. It reports exactly what the notes support and states the limitation honestly.

options.text: Over 30 participants benefited, with strong satisfaction reported.
options.feedback: Not safe. Satisfaction was never measured. That is invented.

options.text: The programme reached 50 people, including indirect beneficiaries.
options.feedback: Not safe. That figure isn't in the notes at all.

missions.hint: Compare each sentence with the field notes. What is a count of people, and what is a count of attendances?
missions.support: If the same person came to both sessions they would be counted twice. So '34' counts visits. Which sentence says that plainly?
missions.explain: Donors trust organisations whose numbers hold up. 'Attendances' with a clear limitation is truthful; anything else claims more than the evidence shows.

advanced.title: Advanced: a lesson plan you can trust
advanced.scenario: Mrs Okoro wants next week's Primary 4 fractions lesson, using bottle tops, in her school's approved format.
items: Paste one old approved lesson plan as the format.
Ask for the fractions lesson in exactly that format, using bottle tops, with no internet needed.
Ask for a simpler version for weak learners and an extension task for fast finishers.
Work every assessment question and answer yourself before the lesson.
Match the plan to the approved scheme of work, then teach it.
advanced.hint: Format first, then the content, then differentiation, then checking.
advanced.support: This is the Day 3 move (format from an accepted example) plus the Day 2 check (verify before it carries your name), applied to a classroom.
advanced.explain: The approved example gives the format, differentiation serves the whole class, and checking every answer yourself is not optional in a classroom.
